scientific_findings: Both paths are fully reliable through t=0.1600149861278153 s. The native004/s2 trace first loses support in the next .004 s saved interval; the exact stride5/s10 trace first records loss in the next .02 s saved interval.

At the first failing transition, all newly unusable seeds are rejected by the local reconstruction-error gate. ESS, rank, anisotropy, support distance, wall blocking, and nonfinite velocity contribute zero native failures; stride has a small g0 residual contribution later in the same .02 s interval, while g1 residual failure remains the cause of every rejected path.

The maximum first-transition support distance is about .00623 m, far below the .03 m support cap, and all replay masks match the terminal trace. This is a reconstruction-residual failure near the evolving interface/velocity branch, not evidence of a support-radius or wall-crossing failure.

The paired curves differ after .16 s, but both end with reliable mass 0 and unknown mass 1. Increasing saved cadence from .02 to .004 while holding the maximum tracer step near .002 s does not resolve the failure; no threshold change is supported.
